purpose: Adds a CodebaseIndex system that syntactically indexes the full checkout (exported symbols, import edges, caller->callee call-graph edges), caches the result per ref under .opencode/codebase-index-cache via atomic writes, and injects a bounded 'Codebase Context (Cross-File Analysis)' section into the review prompt so reviewers can detect cross-file bugs (broken imports, missing exports, renamed-but-unupdated callers), degrading gracefully to a diff-only review on any failure.
riskRationale: The feature is enabled by default (review.enableCodebaseIndex: true) and runs a synchronous full-tree parse on the review hot path. Its headline broken-import detector both misses require()/dynamic import() calls in .ts files and falsely flags legitimate asset/JSON imports; the ref-keyed cache is stored inside the attacker-influenced checkout and its shallow-validated contents are rendered verbatim into the prompt (an implicit prompt-injection channel); and the shipped action bundle roughly triples in size by inlining the TypeScript compiler. These risks are mitigated by try/catch graceful degradation, an off-switch, a self-invalidating cache, and 18+ passing tests; no public API is broken.

text: A well-architected, well-tested feature that matches its stated design: ts.createSourceFile-based extraction is fast (the 10K-file perf test passes), the ref-keyed cache uses atomic temp-file+rename writes with graceful failure, the engine degrades to diff-only review on any indexing error, and 18+ tests cover extraction, cache corruption/invalidation, relevance filtering, prompt injection, and the monorepo integration path. All previously-reported issues (dead regex branch, external-import misclassification, dead config flag, missing callGraph validation, index build placed before the exclude checks) were fixed and verified in this iteration. Remaining concerns are accuracy gaps in the broken-import detector, a cache-in-checkout trust boundary, an event-loop-blocking synchronous index build in the App, and a handful of minor extraction-fidelity and test-quality items.

reasoning: The core mechanism is sound and degrades gracefully, but three important issues remain: the broken-import detector both misses require()/dynamic import() calls in .ts files and falsely flags legitimate asset/JSON imports as broken; the ref-keyed cache is stored inside the attacker-influenced checkout and its shallow-validated contents are injected verbatim into the review prompt (a prompt-injection channel); and the fully synchronous index build blocks the App's event loop on the review hot path. The first two have small, contained fixes, but converting the blocking walk is an architectural change, so the remaining important issues are not all straightforward for an automated agent to resolve safely.

message: Cache writes use a temp file + atomic rename with best-effort cleanup, and get() validates refSha plus all three collections (symbols/imports/callGraph), so a corrupt, partial, or mismatched entry can never break the review; the corrupt/mismatch/partial cases are explicitly covered by tests.

Indexing is gated behind the exclude/skip early-returns and wrapped in try/catch (engine.ts:486-521) with a separately guarded formatContext(), so fully-excluded PRs never pay the indexing cost and any failure degrades to a diff-only review; rooting the index at the git top-level keeps index-relative paths aligned with repo-root-relative ChangedFile.path values in monorepos.

The cache key combining headSha with a git status --porcelain working-tree digest cleanly solves the autofix-loop staleness problem: a clean checkout keeps the stable headSha key, while uncommitted working-tree changes (re-reviews of the same ref) naturally invalidate the cache.

The monorepo integration test exercises the real end-to-end pipeline — resolveCodebaseRoot() rooting the index at the git top-level while workDir is a package subdirectory — and asserts on the actual injected prompt options (codebaseIndexContext contains 'helper'), verifying the full pipeline rather than mocking it away.

getContextForFiles() relevance-filters the full index down to only what touches changed files (verified both positively and negatively in tests), and formatContext() caps each section (100 symbols / 150 edges) with explicit truncation notices, keeping the injected prompt context bounded.

Handling `export default someIdentifier;` by marking the referenced declaration as the default export is a subtle correctness win that prevents the index from falsely reporting a legitimate default export as missing.

The regex fallback runs only when the AST parse returns undefined or the file has a JS-family extension (extractor.ts:118), so .ts/.tsx/.mts/.cts files never receive require()/dynamic import() coverage. Since ts.createSourceFile is error-tolerant and virtually never returns undefined, the comment on lines 113-117 acknowledges the regex pass must run 'in addition' — but it only does so for JS files. A TypeScript file using `const mod = require('./mod')` or `await import('./mod')` produces no import edge, so broken-import detection silently misses dynamic/CommonJS imports in the primary language, contradicting the PR description's claim that these are covered by the regex fallback.
suggestion: Run the require/import regex pass for TypeScript files too, but push only imports (not the module.exports symbols, which the AST pass already extracts from TS) and dedupe against AST import edges by line+specifier as the comment already claims. Add a test with `require('./mod')` inside a .ts file and one with `await import('./mod')` to lock in the behavior.

message: resolveLocalImport only resolves TS/JS-family extensions and index files, so legitimate local imports of non-code assets resolve to '' with isExternal undefined, and formatContext's filter (!edge.targetFile && !edge.isExternal) then renders them in 'Unresolved Local Imports (possible broken imports)'. Common imports like `import data from './data.json'` or `import './styles.css'` are therefore flagged as broken in every review prompt, which can drive the reviewer to report bogus issues. The test fixture at codebase-index.test.ts:86 even imports './side-effect.css' but never asserts that it is not flagged.
suggestion: Classify known non-code asset specifiers (json/css/scss/less/images/fonts/wasm/sourcemaps) as external in isExternalSpecifier so they are excluded from the unresolved-imports section, and add an assertion that the ./side-effect.css fixture is not rendered as broken.

message: The index cache is stored inside the git checkout at workDir/.opencode/codebase-index-cache/<refSha>.json and CodebaseIndexCache.get() (cache.ts:27-47) reads it BEFORE extraction with only a refSha-match + array-shape check. Because the checkout contains attacker-controlled PR content, a malicious PR can commit this file (it knows its own head SHA, which is the clean-tree cache key) with valid-shaped JSON; formatContext() then renders the planted symbol/import/call-edge strings verbatim into the review prompt as the authoritative 'Codebase Context (Cross-File Analysis)' section — a structured, implicitly-trusted prompt-injection channel. Additionally, in CI each run starts from a fresh checkout, so the multi-MB JSON is rebuilt and rewritten every run and only the autofix loop benefits; for repos that do not gitignore .opencode/ the file also pollutes git status output and can be accidentally committed.
suggestion: Store the cache outside the repo tree (e.g., os.tmpdir()/homedir keyed by normalized repo identity + sha), or reject any cache file that is part of the git tree (git ls-files), and validate loaded entries with a strict schema.

message: The codebase index build blocks the Node event loop on the review hot path. CodebaseExtractor.extract() uses only synchronous fs APIs (readdirSync/readFileSync/existsSync/statSync), and engine.ts additionally runs `git rev-parse` (line 262) and `git status --porcelain` (line 288) synchronously via execFileSync, with buildOrLoad() awaiting a method that never yields. In the GitHub Action (a single-purpose process) this is acceptable, but the Probot App is a long-running web server: a multi-second blocking walk on a large repo (the 5s warning at line 511 confirms builds can reach that) stalls every concurrent webhook request for all repos served by the app.
suggestion: Run extraction off the main thread (worker_threads) or convert the walk/parse to async with fs.promises; at minimum, skip the synchronous git-status fingerprint when a cache entry for headSha already exists so a warm cache never pays for a git walk.

message: The comment claims the regex pass is 'Dedupe against AST results by line+specifier', but no dedupe is implemented — regex symbols/imports are pushed unconditionally for every JS file. Reproduced: a .js file containing both a static side-effect `import './helper.js'` and `require('./helper.js')` produces two identical side-effect edges to the same target, which render as duplicate rows in the prompt's Import Relationships section (the CJS test at codebase-index.test.ts:273 only exercises a .cjs file, so it never catches this). The exports regex also fires inside minified bundles (e.g. webpack's `t[n]={exports:{}}` and `e.exports`), so committed bundles like action/lib/index.js generate hundreds of phantom `default` export symbols — this PR's own injected context shows ~740 duplicate `default` entries from that single file, flooding the prompt with meaningless duplicates whenever a bundle is among the changed files.
suggestion: Implement the dedupe the comment promises (skip a regex side-effect edge when an AST edge for the same specifier already exists in the file, keyed by line+specifier+kind), skip the module.exports regex for clearly single-line minified bundles, or cap extracted symbols per file so a bundle cannot dominate the context; add a mixed-syntax .js fixture (static import + require of the same module) asserting a single edge.

message: get() only checks that symbols/imports/callGraph are arrays — it does not validate the contents of each entry. A hand-edited, schema-drifted, or (per the trust-boundary issue above) attacker-supplied entry with array-shaped data but missing fields (e.g. a symbol without name/file/line) passes validation and is rendered into the prompt as 'undefined'/garbage rather than being rejected.
suggestion: Parse cached entries with a strict Zod schema (the shapes already exist as TypeScript interfaces) and return null on any entry-level mismatch, both hardening corruption handling and closing the injection surface.

message: extractRegexBased() applies the require/import/module.exports regexes to the raw file content including comments and string literals, so a commented-out `// require('./x.js')` or a string containing `module.exports =` in a .js/.cjs file produces phantom import edges and phantom exported symbols that are then injected into the review prompt as real code. This degrades the signal-to-noise of the very context the feature exists to provide.
suggestion: Strip comments and string/template literals before matching (e.g., reuse the parsed source file's positions), or restrict the regex scan to code regions.

message: WorkspaceInfo from detectWorkspace() is computed and stored on every index (extractor.ts:703-711) but nothing consumes it — CodebaseIndex.getContextForFiles(), formatContext(), and engine.ts never read data.workspace, so the 'monorepo awareness' is inert. This persisted from the previous review round.
suggestion: Either surface workspace membership in the prompt (e.g., show which workspace package each changed file belongs to), or remove detectWorkspace()/WorkspaceInfo until a real consumer exists (YAGNI).

message: Promoting typescript to a runtime dependency and inlining it via ncc grew the shipped action bundle from ~2.9MB to ~7.9MB (action/lib/index.js, measured at the base commit vs. this branch). Every action run downloads this regardless of whether indexing is used (it defaults on), and the app package now installs the full compiler for npm consumers.
suggestion: Consider a lighter syntactic parser (e.g., @babel/parser) that covers the same symbol/import/call-edge extraction at a fraction of the size, or lazy-load typescript so it is only pulled in when enableCodebaseIndex is on.

message: The mergeRepoConfig JSDoc (config.ts:191-205) states 'Only the review.sensitivity / review.categories blocks are merged ... all other config-file sections remain Action-only', which is now false — review.enableCodebaseIndex is also merged (config.ts:224). Stale documentation that will mislead maintainers reasoning about which repo-config keys reach the engine.
suggestion: Update the JSDoc to include review.enableCodebaseIndex in the list of merged blocks.

message: The new ENABLE_CODEBASE_INDEX env-var parsing (config.ts:66-68) and the mergeRepoConfig propagation (config.ts:211-224) have no test coverage — the app test suite has no config tests, while the PR added tests only in lib. The precedence rule (server env opt-out vs. per-repo enable) is exactly the kind of behavior that silently regresses.
suggestion: Add a small app test asserting that ENABLE_CODEBASE_INDEX=false is overridden by a repo config enableCodebaseIndex:true (and vice-versa when the key is absent), mirroring the existing mergeRepoConfig behavior for sensitivity.

message: The codebase context section is silently dropped in two paths even though the engine already computed it: (1) when effectiveBudgetMode === 'split' — the single-batch path in engine.ts:584-588 still builds the context, yet the builder discards it (builder.ts:263) exactly for the large-PR case where cross-file analysis is most valuable; and (2) whenever a custom reviewPromptFile is configured, because buildReviewPrompt returns early at builder.ts:95-105 before this section, making the default-on feature inert for custom-prompt users.
suggestion: Document the split-mode exclusion (or guard in the engine so the context isn't built when it will be discarded), and append the section after the custom prompt when codebaseIndexContext is provided.

message: The performance sanity check asserts an exact symbol count (toBe(20000)) and a 20s bound that is 4x the documented <5s acceptance criterion (the comment at line 442 acknowledges the target). A real 2-4x indexing regression (e.g., 0.5s -> 6s) would still pass while violating the acceptance criterion, and the exact count makes the test brittle to legitimate symbol-extraction changes.
suggestion: Assert symbols.length toBeGreaterThan(10000) instead of the exact 20000, and tighten the time bound to something closer to the 5s criterion with a modest margin (e.g., 10s), or gate the assertion on the 5s target so the logged value is actionable.

message: The cp.execFileSync mock returns '' for every unhandled git command. If the review pipeline ever depends on another git subcommand, the test will silently pass on fabricated empty output instead of failing loudly, and the mock is never restored within the test (relying on the next beforeEach's vi.resetAllMocks()).
suggestion: Scope the mock to only the commands the pipeline needs (assert git rev-parse --show-toplevel and git status --porcelain were called with the expected cwd), and restore the original implementation in the finally block alongside the temp-dir cleanup.
